help.title: A gentle start
help.macBody: Open HelloBreak, choose apps, and set a daily allowance. Start management. Use the menu bar to stop and remove window covers at any time.
help.chromeBody: Install the local connector, then load the Chrome extension from chrome://extensions in developer mode. Add domains in HelloBreak and check that the extension says Connected. Do not also select the whole browser as an app if you only want website limits.
help.limitBody: HelloBreak is a self-control tool. Window changes can briefly reveal content. Quitting the Mac App ends window covers; an enabled Chrome extension retains known site restrictions until management is stopped. These controls can be bypassed by the device owner.
help.contactBody: Use the project issue tracker for support. Please do not include private conversations or sensitive browsing information.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.summary: HelloBreak stores your rules and connection records on your device. There is no account, advertising SDK, or built-in analytics.
privacy.local: Local data includes selected app tokens or identifiers, website domains, estimated active use, release expiry, your connection menu, self-reported attempts, and local diagnostic state. HelloBreak does not read chats, import contacts, or request proof of social interaction.
privacy.browser: The Chrome extension uses tab, site, idle, storage, redirect, and native messaging permissions. It sends only configured active site hostnames to the Mac App, not paths, queries, or page content. Original URLs stay in the pause tab for restoration. iOS app selection uses Apple’s opaque Screen Time tokens.
privacy.control: You can remove rules and stop management in the App, revoke system permissions, or disable the extension. Local files and browser extension storage remain until you clear them. HelloBreak has no cloud copy; device backups are governed by your system settings.
privacy.web: These static pages do not include analytics or advertising scripts. The hosting provider may process ordinary request metadata, such as IP address, to serve pages. If you contact us through a third-party issue tracker, that service’s privacy policy applies. This policy describes the current development build.
